title: How Cliff Diving Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore cliff diving: personal anecdotes about jumping from local quarries, the Acapulco cliff divers (La Quebrada) and their roughly 135-foot jumps, the legend of King Kahikili of Maui and the Hawaiian cliff-diving tradition, the Timex "takes a licking" watch commercials and ABC's Wide World of Sports popularizing cliff diving, the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Championships and a Napoleon-era fort in France, the physics of free fall (gravity, acceleration, terminal velocity-like deceleration on water entry, weightlessness), dangers such as Rick's Café in Jamaica, safety tips, notable divers Orlando Duque and De Juan Ron (waterfall diving), high diving records, and a listener email about the word "hinky." Note: the transcript is a rough auto-generated text with many misheard names and numbers.

segments.title: Opening banter and personal cliff jumps
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about jumping off cliffs and quarries they have known, and mention the Acapulco divers.

segments.title: Acapulco cliff divers and La Quebrada
segments.summary: The La Quebrada divers in Acapulco jump from roughly 130-150 foot cliffs nightly; the tradition is said to have been started by a boy, and the hosts describe the setting.

segments.title: Origins: King Kahikili and Hawaiian cliff diving
segments.summary: Legend credits King Kahikili of Maui with jumping from a cliff around 1770; the hosts describe the Hawaiian tradition and its nightly reenactment at Maui.

segments.title: Popularization: Timex commercials and ABC Wide World of Sports
segments.summary: Timex watch commercials showed watches surviving cliff dives, and ABC's Wide World of Sports in the 1960s helped popularize cliff diving as a televised sport.

segments.title: Red Bull championships and Napoleon-era fort
segments.summary: The hosts preview the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Championships and mention divers jumping from an old Napoleonic fort off the coast of France.
topics: Red Bull Cliff Diving World Championships

segments.title: Physics of free fall and water entry
segments.summary: Explanation of gravity, constant acceleration of about 9.8 m/s per second, the effect of cliff height on speed, the danger of deceleration at water entry, weightlessness during the fall, and Galileo's and Apollo 15's demonstration that mass does not change fall rate.

segments.title: Dangers, safety tips, and notable divers
segments.summary: Discussion of injuries from belly flops (including a Rick's Cafe case), safety advice such as checking the water and diving with a friend, competition scoring, and divers Orlando Duque and De Juan Ron.
